title: The completion matrix validator: the ledger's own guards
note: This file is not a subsystem, it is the thing that decides whether the other rows are telling the truth -- so it is in the trust boundary for every completion claim this repository makes, and a guard here that quietly stopped working would be invisible in exactly the way that matters most. C1-C4 attack the boundary vocabulary, which is the cheapest available route to a finished matrix over an unfinished system: move a sentence from residual_gaps to boundaries and the row goes COMPLETE with nothing else changed. C5-C8 attack the checks that keep a row's evidence its own -- COMPLETE with gaps still listed, COMPLETE with no mutation coverage, borrowed coverage, a hosted claim with no run behind it. C9-C10 attack the two staleness guards, which exist because twelve rows were once found describing subsystems that had been built months earlier. C9 was rewritten and C13-C18 added with D-2026-44. The old C9 anchored on the rule 'hosted_ci must contain a run id', which was deleted: that rule was satisfied by a sentence denying a hosted run while naming one, so it certified 14 rows as having evidence they had never had. The evidence axis it was replaced by is checkable, and these mutations attack each part of it -- the prose contradiction, the missing commit, the missing digest, absence inside the digest, directory membership, and the two ways the derived verdict can be made to assert instead of measure.

mutations.name: C1_a_boundary_may_describe_work
mutations.find:
for phrase in _WORK_PHRASES:
                if phrase in low:
mutations.rationale: 'not implemented' becomes a stateable limit, and every unfinished row can be closed by moving one sentence between two fields

mutations.name: C2_absent_testing_is_a_limit_under_any_reason
mutations.find: if hit and reason not in _TESTABILITY_REASONS:
mutations.rationale: 'architecturally intended' starts explaining why a test was never written, which it cannot do: it explains absent behaviour, not absent coverage of behaviour that is there

mutations.name: C3_every_reason_can_excuse_absent_testing
mutations.rationale: same loophole as C2 by the other route, and the more likely one: widening a set reads as tidying up

mutations.name: C4_a_boundary_needs_no_argument
mutations.find: if not isinstance(detail, str) or len(detail.strip()) < 80:
mutations.replace: if not isinstance(detail, str) or len(detail.strip()) < 0:
mutations.rationale: a boundary becomes an assertion with nothing behind it, which is how unfinished work gets reclassified as a limit of what is possible

mutations.name: C5_a_detail_may_restate_the_limit
mutations.find: elif detail.strip() in limit or limit.strip() in detail:
mutations.rationale: the evidence requirement is satisfied by copying the claim into the evidence field

mutations.name: C6_complete_may_keep_its_residual_gaps
mutations.rationale: the one arithmetic relation the whole matrix rests on -- COMPLETE means no gaps -- stops being enforced, and 39/39 can be declared over a list of open work

mutations.name: C7_complete_needs_no_mutation_coverage
mutations.rationale: a row can claim completion with tests that would pass if the enforcement they cover were deleted

mutations.name: C8_complete_needs_no_boundaries
mutations.find:
if not bounds:
                    # The classification says
mutations.rationale: the classification says 'complete to current technically defensible LIMIT' and the limit stops having to be stated, which is the easiest way to overstate a system

mutations.name: C9_a_row_with_no_run_may_name_one_in_its_prose
mutations.rationale: the exact defect the old rule was defeated by comes back: 'pending: added after run 33939090740' is a sentence saying no hosted run covers this row, and it passes a check about citing runs because it names one while denying it. It is how 14 rows were classified COMPLETE

mutations.name: C10_stale_prose_about_built_subsystems_is_accepted
mutations.find:
named = {m for m in modules
                         if len(m) > 4 and m in low}
mutations.rationale: restores the state twelve rows were found in: 'the scheduler does not exist yet', months after it did

mutations.name: C11_stale_coverage_claims_are_accepted
mutations.find: hits = {t for t in _fuzz_targets() if _fuzz_gap_names(low, t)}
mutations.rationale: a row stays out of COMPLETE for fuzzing that was already written, which understates the system while looking rigorous

mutations.name: C12_borrowed_mutation_coverage_is_accepted
mutations.rationale: a row cites a spec that mutates somebody else's code, and the coverage claim is about a file the row does not own

mutations.name: C13_a_run_may_be_cited_with_no_commit
mutations.rationale: a run id with no commit behind it is accepted, which is the state 21 rows were in: a citation that cannot be checked against any code because nothing records which code it ran on

mutations.name: C14_a_commit_may_be_cited_with_no_digest
mutations.rationale: evidence names a commit but records nothing recomputable, so the covers/predates question can never be asked and the row reads as verified by default

mutations.name: C15_absence_is_not_part_of_the_implementation_digest
mutations.find:
h.update(b"\x00ABSENT\x00" if blob is None
                 else b"\x00" + hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest().encode())
mutations.replace:
if blob is not None:
            h.update(b"\x00" + hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest().encode())
mutations.rationale: a file that did not exist at the cited commit hashes as though it did, so the 33 rows naming implementation files that postdate their run would read as covered

mutations.name: C16_a_named_directory_is_digested_without_its_members
mutations.find:
members = listdir(p)
        expanded.extend(members if members else [p])
mutations.rationale: rows name tools/mutations, and a spec added to it since the run is exactly the coverage the run did not have; collapsing the directory to its own name hides that

mutations.name: C17_every_row_derives_COVERS
mutations.find:
return (EV_COVERS if now == ev.get("implementation_sha256")
            else EV_PREDATES)
mutations.rationale: the evidence axis stops measuring and starts asserting; the summary then reports 39/39 covered while nothing was recomputed

mutations.name: C18_unresolvable_evidence_is_reported_as_stale
mutations.find:
if not ev.get("commit") or ev.get("commit") == "UNRECORDED" \
            or not ev.get("implementation_sha256"):
        return EV_UNRESOLVABLE
mutations.replace:
if not ev.get("commit") or ev.get("commit") == "UNRECORDED" \
            or not ev.get("implementation_sha256"):
        return EV_PREDATES
mutations.rationale: 'I cannot tell whether this is stale' is reported as 'I checked and it is stale', which claims a measurement nobody made -- the same overclaim the axis exists to stop
